status: SEPARATE from the frozen five-model primary validation -- does not modify it

frozen_primary_reference.note: These files are READ ONLY inputs to this experiment. Hashes of all frozen primary files were recorded before this run and will be re-verified after, to prove nothing was modified.

scientific_question: Do predictions from an unseen OpenAI model become more reliable when they agree with claims that receive higher scores under the pre-existing frozen five-model reliability framework? This is NOT a new benchmark of OpenAI models and NOT a new primary endpoint.

openai_model.selection_rationale: Most recent dated (non-aliased) stable flagship chat-completion snapshot available via /v1/models at run time; standard tier (not -pro/-mini/-nano, not a reasoning model), closest usage-pattern match to the 5 frozen models. Selected by the user after being presented with 3 options (gpt-5.5-2026-04-23, gpt-5-2025-08-07, o3-2025-04-16) due to genuine ambiguity in model choice.
openai_model.api: client.chat.completions.create (same API surface as the frozen 5-model experiment)

generation_parameters.max_tokens_note: The frozen experiment used max_tokens=512. This model REJECTS 'max_tokens' entirely (400 error: 'Unsupported parameter: max_tokens is not supported with this model. Use max_completion_tokens instead.'). max_completion_tokens=512 is used instead -- same numeric budget, renamed parameter, confirmed empirically before the run.
generation_parameters.temperature_note: Empirically confirmed via a probe call: 'Unsupported value: temperature does not support 0.0 with this model. Only the default (1) value is supported.' The frozen experiment used temperature=0.0. This model does not allow overriding temperature at all. This is a genuine, disclosed deviation -- NOT emulated or worked around.
generation_parameters.top_p_note: Confirmed via probe call that top_p is accepted by the API, but left unset to match the frozen script's convention of not overriding it, and because temperature cannot be controlled anyway.
generation_parameters.seed_note: Confirmed via a two-call reproducibility probe (identical prompt, identical seed) that this model DOES return identical output under a fixed seed, despite temperature being fixed at its default. This is the closest available approximation to 'deterministic/low-variance' for this model.
generation_parameters.system_message: none -- matches the frozen P1-P4 construction, where the full instruction is a single user-role message (no separate system role used anywhere in llm_prompting.py / llm_prompting_heldout.py).

prompts.reuse_method: Imported directly via importlib from llm_prompting_heldout.py at run time -- NOT retyped or recreated -- to guarantee byte-identical P1-P4 prompt text and few-shot examples.
prompts.p5_status: P5_selection does not exist anywhere in llm_prompting_heldout.py (verified in the prior frozen-run preflight) -- structurally impossible to invoke from the imported function.

held_out_set.note: Identical file already used for the frozen 5-model run; reused as-is, not modified or regenerated.

planned_calls: 243 proteins x 3 namespaces x 4 prompts x 1 model = 2,916
namespace_note: The user's original instruction stated '243 x 4 = 972' calls, but the frozen P1-P4 prompts are namespace-specific (build_prompts(entry, namespace, ...)). This discrepancy was flagged and resolved by explicit user decision: the OpenAI run follows the SAME convention as the frozen 5-model experiment (243 x 3 namespaces x 4 prompts = 2,916 calls), producing namespace-labeled claims directly comparable to the existing pooled claim set.

output_structure.raw: raw/ -- one JSONL file, full API response records per call
output_structure.parsed: parsed/ -- parsed GO claims per call
output_structure.analysis: analysis/ -- derived tables (frozen-score-vs-correctness, overlap, organism/namespace breakdowns, bootstrap CIs)
output_structure.logs: logs/ -- run logs, including every failure and retry

no_leakage_commitment: OpenAI results will not be used to select the model (already selected before any scientific call), tune the reliability score, change weights/thresholds/prompts, remove proteins, change the held-out cohort, alter the primary endpoint, or redefine correctness. Any problem found will be reported, not silently worked around by changing the above.
